title: Reduced locally quasi-finite spaces over a field are unions of finite field spectra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose $X$ is reduced, meaning an etale scheme atlas has local rings without nonzero nilpotents, and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally quasi-finite, meaning that every etale scheme chart has locally quasi-finite structural morphism [pqf-def-quasifinite]. There are a set $I$, field extensions $K_i/k$ with $\dim_k K_i<\infty$ for every $i\in I$, and an isomorphism of algebraic spaces over $k$ $$X\simeq\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}K_i.$$ The coproduct is the disjoint union of the represented schemes, regarded as an algebraic space. No quasi-compactness, separatedness or perfectness of $k$ is assumed; $I$ may be empty or infinite.

source.place: Tag 06S0 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-over-field), (1) implies (5), specialized to reduced spaces: each local Artinian algebra in (5) is reduced and hence a field.

proof.text: Choose an etale scheme atlas $U\to X$. Let $V\to X$ be any etale scheme chart; its structural map $f:V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally quasi-finite by hypothesis, hence locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type]. Let $v\in V$. By the definition [pqf-def-quasifinite] there are an affine open $v\in\operatorname{Spec}A=W\subseteq V$ and an affine open of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ containing $f(W)$; the one-point space $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has itself as only nonempty open, so the ring map is $\varphi:k\to A$, of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime $\mathfrak q$ of $v$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-quasifinite-zero-fibre-dimension] to $\varphi$: here $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=(0)$, $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=k$ and $F=A\otimes_kk\cong A$ with $\overline{\mathfrak q}\mapsto\mathfrak q$, so $\dim_{\mathfrak q}\operatorname{Spec}A=0$. By [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] the open neighbourhoods of $v$ in $W$ are open neighbourhoods of $v$ in $V$ with the same subspace topology, so $0\le\dim_vV\le\dim_vW=0$. In the chart definition of dimension recalled in [lem-sfb-zero-dimensional-field-space-components] (the same infimum over open neighbourhoods), every local dimension of $X$ is therefore zero, so $\dim X\le0$; the empty case has empty supremum. Local finite type is likewise tested on these charts.

source.place: Tag 06S0 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-over-field), proof of (1) implies (2); chartwise use of morphisms.tex Tag 0397 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0) in its affine ring form over the field k.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-zero-dimensional-field-space-components] with $K=k$. The preceding step verifies its local finite type and dimension hypotheses, with no separation assumption. Obtain a scheme representing $X$ and an isomorphism over $k$, $X\simeq\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, where every $A_i$ is nonzero, local, Artinian and finite-dimensional over $k$. This includes an arbitrary set of components, and the empty space gives $I=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 06S0 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-over-field), (2) implies (4) implies (5), through Tag 06LZ (lemma-locally-finite-type-dim-zero) and varieties.tex Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0).

proof.text: Retain the reduced atlas $U\to X$ supplied by the hypothesis. Now that $X$ is a scheme this is an etale morphism of schemes, hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. It is still surjective. The descent assertion of [lem-sfb-space-smooth-reduced-locality] makes the represented scheme $X$ reduced. For every open component $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, its local rings are the local rings of $X$ there, and are reduced. The local-ring/section equivalence of [def-pc-reduced-scheme] makes $A_i=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A_i,\mathcal O)$ reduced.

source.place: Tag 06S0 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-over-field), reduced specialization of (5); reducedness descent: spaces-descent.tex Tag 0GB3 (lemma-reduced-local-smooth); schemes.tex Tag 01J1 (lemma-reduced).

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product] to $A_i$. Since it is nonzero and local, its set of maximal ideals consists of its unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_i$. Thus the canonical product isomorphism is the quotient isomorphism $A_i\simeq A_i/\mathfrak m_i$ onto a field. Give the same ring $A_i$ the transported field structure and call it $K_i$. Its existing unital $k$-algebra map is injective: its kernel is an ideal of the field $k$, and cannot contain $1$ because $A_i\ne0$. Hence $K_i/k$ is a field extension, and $\dim_k K_i=\dim_k A_i<\infty$. The rings and structural maps have not changed, so the coproduct isomorphism of step 2 is exactly the required isomorphism over $k$. No separability of these extensions is claimed.
